title: Dependency-Scoped Transactional Continual Learning

research_transition.from: Core Validation 002/002B/002C studied precise functional write-addressability.
research_transition.to: 003 tests whether sparse routing can make continual-learning safety a local validation problem even when updates are ordinary gradient training.
research_transition.rule: 003 is a new systems/mechanism validation and cannot relabel prior frozen outcomes.

hypotheses.H1: With a frozen router and frozen shared parameters, changing only routed expert blocks must leave historical computations whose routes do not intersect those blocks unchanged.
hypotheses.H2: The pre-update routing trace can define a dependency-scoped regression set whose PASS decision agrees with a hidden full-history oracle with false-safe rate <= 1%.
hypotheses.H3: Transactional commit should reduce cumulative positive old-regression damage versus always committing the same local update while retaining useful new-learning gain.
hypotheses.H4: Finer independently routed blocks should reduce dependency coverage and candidate-state size enough to create a useful granularity/cost frontier.
hypotheses.H5: A controlled router-drift stress should demonstrate why dependency indexes require a stable routing plane; this is diagnostic and does not veto the core frozen-router mechanism.

scope.router_specialization: favorable structured router: each context composes two shared functional families and is hashed to one replica inside each family
scope.primary_question: Can sparse routing convert global continual-learning regression safety into dependency-scoped local validation with transactional commit?

world.base_behavior: Each context is a convex composition of two shared nonlinear basis functions.
world.new_knowledge: Each mutable context has a fixed private nonlinear residual function whose amplitude increases when that context receives a transaction.
world.anchor_rule: The first 16 contexts never receive updates and provide an invariant forgetting probe.

model.type: single sparse routed expert layer with shared content trunk
model.granularity_rule: At granularity g there are 4g experts and each expert hidden width is 64/g. Total expert hidden/parameter budget is approximately constant while a context still routes to exactly two blocks.
model.active_compute_note: Logical active expert parameters decrease with finer granularity; this is intentional and is reported as part of the cost/plasticity frontier rather than hidden as a confound.
model.shared_parameters: content trunk and shared head are trained during pretraining, then frozen for local variants

continual_stream.stream_rule: The 48 mutable contexts are traversed in independently shuffled epochs, so 96 transactions update every mutable context twice.
continual_stream.finite_data_rule: Each transaction receives one fixed 32-example training set; optimization reuses that same set for all 24 steps.

variant_definitions.standard_moe_always: Update shared trunk/head plus routed experts and always commit.
variant_definitions.local_always: Freeze shared state/router, update only routed experts, always commit.
variant_definitions.local_tx_frozen: Same local candidate as local_always, but commit only if new gain and dependency-scoped old regression pass.
variant_definitions.local_tx_router_drift: Same as local_tx_frozen, then perturb the router before validation to stress a stale pre-update dependency index.

router_drift_stress.rule: Add deterministic Gaussian noise to all replica-router vectors and renormalize before candidate validation. This is a causal stress control, not a model of a particular router optimizer.

evaluation.dependency_scope: Historical sample x is locally tested iff its pre-update route intersects any expert touched by the current transaction; current target-context samples are excluded because their old behavior is intentionally superseded.
evaluation.hidden_global_scope: All historical samples except the target context. It is evaluator-only and never influences commit.
evaluation.new_gain: [MSE_before(new truth)-MSE_candidate(new truth)] / E[(y_new-y_old)^2], measured on an independent 128-example set.
evaluation.false_safe: local PASS but hidden global oracle FAIL.
evaluation.structural_escape: Fraction of out-of-scope historical samples whose candidate prediction changes by >1e-6.
evaluation.candidate_state_fraction: Parameter count of touched expert blocks divided by total model parameter count.
evaluation.cost_proxy: Per transaction candidate_state_fraction + dependency_coverage; summed and divided by accepted updates.
evaluation.final_anchor_retention: Normalized MSE on never-updated anchor contexts.
evaluation.final_mutable_fit: Normalized MSE on all mutable contexts under the final truth.

gates.rule: A fixed granularity g>1 must pass every core gate in all formal seeds. Router-drift stress is diagnostic only.

interpretation_limits: This is a favorable synthetic mechanism test, not evidence that natural-language MoE routers already create suitable dependency domains.
Positive H1/H2 results rely on a stable pre-update routing plane and frozen shared parameters in the local candidate.
Granularity changes logical active expert compute as well as block size; the experiment reports the resulting cost/plasticity frontier rather than claiming a pure block-size causal effect.
The hidden global oracle is run only for scientific measurement and must never be used by the transactional commit decision.
A negative result rejects this frozen structured-routing mechanism and gate set, not all forms of transactional continual learning.
